title: Identificação dos parâmetros de estabilidade e controle do aeromodelo VR-01
relevance: An unusually direct RC-model-airplane identification case: the UnB Air Robotics Lab's 2.4 kg, approximately 1.98 m-span VR-01 was instrumented for longitudinal and lateral-directional maneuvers. The abstract specifies elevator pulse/doublet, aileron bank-to-bank, rudder doublet, measured angular rates, attitudes, angle of attack, sideslip, and airspeed; it reports that the estimated models did not adequately fit the real aircraft.
limitations: The thesis reports a negative identification result, not a usable coefficient set. Its abstract attributes difficulty to gusts, pilot workload, trouble holding trim, limited or asynchronous sensor sampling, and other flight/data-processing issues. Full text was not acquired, so no result beyond the official record and indexed abstract is asserted.

title: Estudo de uma configuração de asa voadora usando o software de CFD OpenFOAM
relevance: Compares steady incompressible OpenFOAM force estimates for a blended-wing-body flying-wing configuration with an earlier experimental wind-tunnel dataset. The thesis sweeps angle of attack from 0° to 17° and identifies solver non-convergence and divergence from experiment above about 10°, where separated flow becomes oscillatory. This is a useful warning about relying on steady CFD near stall.
limitations: The author did not conduct a new wind-tunnel or flight campaign; the measurements come from the earlier Hernan (2008) experiment. The geometry is a BWB research configuration, not a hobby flying wing. The USP use notice restricts the document to private research/teaching and citation and reserves reproduction, so the local copy stays ignored and private.

title: Aplicação da identificação de sistemas para estimação das derivadas de estabilidade e controle de aeronaves de asa fixa
relevance: Uses recorded real flight-test data attributed to Suit (1972) for a Ryan Navion to estimate 22 of 35 stability/control derivatives by least squares, then checks the model through six-degree-of-freedom trajectory reconstruction. It gives a Portuguese-language worked example of the data-to-model process, including advice on doublet and 3-2-1-1 maneuvers and sensor calibration.
limitations: This is a full-scale Navion dataset, not an RC airplane, and the thesis author reanalyzes historical data rather than conducting a new test campaign. The method assumes local linear behavior near an operating point; do not extend its reconstructed model to deep stall or transfer its derivatives to a trainer. The raw Suit dataset is not bundled with this thesis.

title: Identificação do modelo da dinâmica longitudinal de uma aeronave não tripulada
relevance: A detailed Portuguese-language worked example of maneuver selection, output-error estimation, and proof-of-match for the 8.87 kg, 4 m-span, high-aspect-ratio EOLO. The thesis is unusually clear that its identified response is fitted to simulator-generated data and cannot establish the aircraft's real aerodynamic parameters.
limitations: This is simulation-based identification and self-consistency checking, not flight validation. The thesis describes instrumentation and a prior flexible-wing test campaign, but those measurements are not the data used for this identification. Its conclusion says real flight measurements are required to identify EOLO's real aerodynamics.

title: Sistema de aquisição de dados de voo de um veículo aéreo não tripulado, Vector-P
relevance: Documents the Vector-P data-acquisition setup: CompactRIO, Crossbow inertial sensors, an air-data boom, GPS, and measured servo positions. It proposes bank-to-bank aileron pulses and rudder doublets/Dutch-roll excitation, making it a concise source for planning inputs and actuator logging.
limitations: The stated objective and future-tense maneuver description show that this paper plans a lateral-directional campaign; it does not present the resulting new flight dataset or fitted lateral derivatives. Vector-P is an institutional UAV, not a sport RC airplane. A separate 2013 Vector-P thesis based on flight-test data is listed below; the 2018 lateral paper is already registered in the legacy source inventory and is not duplicated here.

title: Identificação da dinâmica e controle por alocação de autoestrutura para pouso automático de Mini-VANT em pista curta com aproximação 3D
relevance: The aircraft is explicitly the commercially available Hangar-9 Alpha60 RC trainer. Its aerodynamic characteristics were determined from wind-tunnel tests and combined with CAD/CFD information to form a model for a coupled descending-turn/short-field approach; the thesis abstract reports simulated landing distances of 235–329 m across wind cases.
limitations: The automatic-landing results are simulation evaluations, not flight-test validation of the model or controller. Full text was not available from the ITA archive during this retrieval, so detailed tunnel conditions, coefficient values and uncertainty are not asserted.

title: Modelo matemático para un vehículo aéreo no tripulado de ala fija, usando un estimador de parámetros ‘filtro de Kalman’
relevance: Describes the six-degree-of-freedom model for Colombia's AURA fixed-wing UAV and uses an extended Kalman filter to estimate aerodynamic parameters. The article's identification tests generate simulated flight data, so it is useful as a model/algorithm example in Spanish rather than as measured flight validation.
limitations: The paper explicitly labels its identification tests as simulated; it does not establish real-flight coefficient accuracy. It is a research UAV, not a hobby sport airframe. The official PDF text was accessible through web indexing, but the local official-PDF transfer timed out, so no local copy was retained.

title: Estimación de parámetros de un UAV tipo ala volante mediante algoritmos metaheurísticos
relevance: Presents MATLAB/Simulink genetic-algorithm and particle-swarm estimators for a flying-wing UAV gray-box model. The reported tests use perturbed simulator-generated data, focus on longitudinal conditions, and compare estimates for 11 parameters against known/theoretical values; this is useful for estimator and observability methodology, not flight evidence.
limitations: The authors explicitly describe real flight data as future work and identify collection of suitable experimental data as a major challenge. It therefore does not validate the estimator against measured aircraft behavior. The official repository endpoint returned an anti-bot challenge to the local downloader, so the original was not saved locally.
